body: shrimp.rs: `gh_mineral_factor` is now double-counted in spawning. It was added to `reproductive_readiness_factors` (line 1478, the new 8th factor feeding the EMA readiness index), but `f_mineral` is still multiplied directly in `spawn_rate` at line 731 (`base_spawn_rate * spawn_readiness * f_mineral`). This means poor mineral conditions have a squared suppressive effect on spawning — once through the smoothed EMA, once through the direct multiplier. Either remove `minerals` from `reproductive_readiness_factors` (keeping only the direct path, matching pre-change behavior), or remove the direct `f_mineral` from `spawn_rate` (letting the EMA handle it). The same double-counting also applies to hatch rate (line 890) where `f_mineral` appears directly while the EMA readiness is not used — but hatch rate is a separate path so only spawning is affected.
